title: Capacity Concierge: Tiered reserved units, autoscale governance & contract QnA
creator: Maria Chen
description: Design and validate a new packaging approach ("Capacity Concierge") for Dedicated that simplifies reserved capacity procurement and adds a predictable autoscale governance model. Deliverables: pricing matrix, contract Q&A answers for enterprise buyers, pilot offer for 2-3 customers, and ops runbook for burst metering and settlement.
objectives: Create a tiered reserved unit (RU) model that maps to common throughput lanes (low/medium/high) across regions
Define autoscale governance: minute-level burst gating, overflow lanes, and automated grace windows
Produce an enterprise-ready Q&A / contract appendix covering preemption policy, data residency, telemetry, and KMS integration
Run a small pricing experiment (A/B) with pilot customers to validate price elasticity and adoption friction
proposed_pricing_matrix: Compact Tier (RU-XS): 1 RU = 1 vGPU-equivalent throughput lane; monthly base $1,200 per RU; 10% overage at per-unit rate
Stable Tier (RU-S): monthly base $3,400 per RU; includes 4 hours/month free burst credits; overage billed per-minute at $0.15/min per RU
Throughput Tier (RU-M): monthly base $7,500 per RU; includes 12 hours/month burst credits and prioritized failover; lower overage $0.08/min per RU
Concierge Add-on: premium SLAs, onboarding, and dedicated support bundle: add $2,500/month per agreement
contract_qna_checklist: Preemption behavior and guaranteed throughput lanes: define soft vs hard preemption windows
Burst metering methodology: how minutes are measured and reconciled
Data residency and encryption: confirm SOC2, KMS integration option, and regional isolation
Auditability: logs, request traces, and token-level cost reports required for compliance reviews
Upgrade and downgrade mechanics: cooling periods, prorations, and crediting rules
Support SLAs and financial SLA credits matrix per tier
acceptance_criteria: Pricing matrix reviewed and signed off by Finance and Sales Ops
Contract Q&A appendix drafted and approved by Legal & Security
Pilot plan with 2 customers agreed, instrumented, and scheduled for 6-week run
Ops runbook for burst metering + settlement published in Confluence
Telemetry hooks for RU utilization, burst minutes, and preemption events instrumented in console
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers find RU abstraction confusing -> Mitigation: publish RU-to-throughput mapping examples and an online calculator
Risk: Burst metering disputes -> Mitigation: provide per-minute stamped usage logs and an audit export for customers
Risk: Pricing undercuts existing large-seat customers -> Mitigation: grandfathering rules and custom negotiation template
Risk: Security questionnaire objections (KMS, logging) -> Mitigation: pre-approved language and fallback integrations
test_plan: Run A/B with two pilot cohorts: cohort A (per-RU with burst credits), cohort B (flat reserved + higher overage)
Measure conversion from pilot to paid (target 30% trial -> paid within 90 days)
Monitor latency and unit cost delta for autoscale events to ensure <=10% cost variance
Collect qualitative feedback from pilot customers on contract clarity and procurement friction
